# Review — cid-tiradas-44-48 (tiradas 44–48, lines 836–898 incl. 875b–875e, 896b–896c)

Adversarial review against the pinned packet, Pidal's rubrics and footnotes on the scan (PDF pp. 185–189, read on
the image at 150 dpi, with crops at 600 dpi for vídolos (v. 873), the italic name in v. 890, pie[de]s (v. 879),
aun (v. 885) and the italic lines 875b/875e), conventions.md, the pilot (01-04) and the preceding parts (35-39,
40-43). All edits made by script (json load/dump, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1). No `t` changed: the 69 `t` lines
concatenated equal the packet's 69 lines exactly (checked by script after the edits); one `l` line per `t` line in
all 26 units.

Checked and found sound (no change):
- Rubrics against the scan: 44 El Cid vende Alcocer a los moros; 45 Venta de Alcocer. (Repetición.); 46 Abandono de
  Alcocer. Buenos agüeros. — El Cid se asienta en el Poyo sobre Monreal; 47 Minaya llega ante el Rey. — Este
  perdona a Minaya, pero no al Cid; 48 El Rey permite a los castellanos irse con el Cid. Assonances right: 44 á-a,
  45 í-o, 46 á (aves á-e), 47 á-a, 48 á (heredades, Fáñez á-e).
- Pidal's footnotes are reported correctly: 836 ('por la mañana se fué Minaya', comp. 827), 842 (Entre pleonastic,
  191; Terrer la casa 'la población de Terrer', 1232), 850 (the proverb and both variants, quoted accurately), 856
  (comp. 802 and p. 59, n. 1), 859 (buenas aves = bona avis, 'buenos agüeros', p. 18, n. 2), 863 (Monreal del Campo,
  Jiloca, seventeen hours from Calatayud), 864 (El Poyo, left of the Jiloca, road Sagunto–Calatayud v. 644, 1227 m,
  El Poyo de mio Cid v. 902, Fuero de Molina, the distances), 869 (Celfa, hoy Cella, 644), 879 ('os pide que', 179),
  881 ('es muy pronto'), 883 (tres sedmanas indefinite; eighteen weeks, 573, 664; five or six months), 887 (honores
  e tierras, 3413; condonar 'conceder, restituir'; comp. 230, 289, 893, 1363-64), 893 (heredades not confiscated;
  comp. 887). There are no footnotes on 841 (sanó), 847 (pago), 892 (huyar) or 896 (feches), and the notes do not
  claim any.
- Italics/restorations checked on the image: f[o] (836, 884), [fincó y] (both words), Ter[rer], [ha], ven[d]ido,
  s[o]s, finca[mo]s, D[a]roca, R[o]y (870, 875), ví[d]olos, su[e], pie[de]s, ay[a]des, se[d]manas, [Álbar Fáñez]
  (whole name). 875b, 875c, 875d, 875e, 896b and 896c are wholly italic on the scan and unnumbered: Pidal's margin
  has 875 at "—Mio Çid Roy Díaz" and 880 at "quel ayades", so 876–880 follow the four italic lines; 895 is at
  "Grado e graçias" and 900 at "aquel poyo", so 897–898 follow 896b–c. The notes say all this, and that the
  letters are ours. The overflow "[taja;" of presentaja (v. 884) set at the end of v. 883 is described correctly.
  pago (847) is unaccented on the scan.
- Flagged points: 836 mañánas (accent as printed; adverbial -s) right; 841 sanó 'recovered' right (Fáriz wounded at
  v. 760); 847 pago read as pagó, compare v. 806, right; 853 vaste = te vas; 862 ivas = íbase; 863 y ffincó, y
  'there' with 'and' left open (kept); 873 ví[d]olos now confirmed; 881 mucho es mañana follows Pidal; 892 huyar
  'to help', hedged; 896 feches as a reduced fazedes, al 'the rest', feredes future of fer: right and hedged where
  needed.
- Grammar labels: aguisado, f[o] (ir/ser), aguardavan, consejavan (reflexive), metudo (-udo participle), vendido les
  a (participle first), fechos los ha (agreement with object), fallariedes (conditional -iedes), tomáronse a +
  inf., váyante (pres. subj. + te), finca[mo]s, compeçaron de, ovo, plogo, fazié (-ié), sabet, tenié, aya
  (optative), ido es (ser auxiliary), enpresentava, cinxo, ayrastes (-astes), sue (fem. possessive), ay[a]des,
  acogello (r > l), prendo, avellas (aved + las), venit, do, quisieren (fut. subj.), far, suéltoles/quítoles,
  feredes, guisaremos, fagades, déxenvos (pres. subj. 3rd pl.), si'nulla. All right.
- House renderings: "who girded on his sword in a good hour" (875, as in 35-39); Minaya Álvar Fáñez in `i`, Álbar
  in `l`; Castile, Vivar, Calatayud, Jalón, Monreal in `i`; "my Çid"; sin/si'nulla dubda 'without fear' as decided
  in 40-43. Nothing bowdlerized.

Findings refused:
- 836 note calls Pidal's written accent in mañánas "unexpected": it marks the stress where it falls, but it is
  indeed unexpected in his orthography. Left.
- 863 note leaves y 'and' open beside y 'there': Pidal writes the conjunction e, but y 'and' is in the known
  glossary as a rarer spelling. The note prefers 'there'. Left.
- 889 `l` "I not to-you I-say nothing" doubles the pronoun: yo is explicit in the line and `l` stays readable. Left.
- 849 `l` "among all the his-men": the house article + possessive rendering. Left.
- 892 huyar: I did not add a lemma (uviar is possible but not supported by any footnote on the scan); the note's
  caution stands.

Checked: the gloss keys (82, excluding __broaden__) equal the novel-forms.json keys exactly. Every __broaden__ value
(31) begins with the known-forms.json entry exactly, then " · " (checked by script). Every token of the 69 lines
(brackets stripped, lowercased, split at the apostrophe: si'nulla → si, nulla) is covered by known + gloss. The
si'nulla handling via `si` (sin with -n assimilated before n-) is right. The mont/real split (Mont Real → mont
broaden + real 'royal') is right. The other entries were checked against the text and found right in lemma,
person, number, tense and mood: mañánas, sobejana, aguardavan, consejavan, asmado, vendido, fallariedes, mesquino,
bive, deliçio, quexar, vaste, váyante, quitó, compeçaron, aves, alcocer, fazié, ivas, ffincó, poyo, real, nulla,
terçera, ido, enpresentava, sonrrisava, llegava, lidiava, ondrado, enbía, bésavos, amas, acogello, sobresto,
honores, venit, quisieren, suéltoles, quítoles, besóle, natural, feches (hedged), feredes, nós, vós, guisaremos,
déxenvos; broadens fo, el, fincó, mala, mas, ha, qué, sos, en, aguijó, al, mucho, mañana, pro, sobre, enantes, desí,
tenié, aya, fermoso, mensaje, cabo, quito, do. No other broaden is missing: casa 'town', part 'side', carta 'deed',
mano 'power', grado, merçed, paria, dubda 'fear', y 'there', la 'the one (of)' are already in the known entries.

Findings refused:
- feches "a reduced form of fazedes … the exact derivation less so": hedged, and nothing is invented. Left.
- váyante "= que te vayan, que te acompañen": loose but not wrong. Left.
- bésavos, suéltoles, besóle give the dative as "your/their/his": the possessive dative, the right sense here. Left.
- Several entries quote the line as an example: the house format; the meaning given is general to the form. Left.
